summary: The ancestor-kind mutation proof is not a kill on Python 3.13: the fault is refused by Path.resolve(strict=True) before the ancestors() S_ISDIR guard it claims to exercise.
failure_scenario: Python 3.13 (allowed by requires-python >=3.11) runs test_removed_runbook_guard_is_assertion_killed[...ancestor-kind]. The mutant drops `stat.S_ISDIR` from ancestors(), yet directory(w) still raises NotADirectoryError inside os.path.realpath(strict=True) because the patched lstat reports 'operator' as S_IFREG. The refusal test therefore still passes, pytest.raises(AssertionError) does not fire, and the test fails with 'DID NOT RAISE'. On 3.11/3.12 the realpath walk does not trip, so the proof passes only because of interpreter-internal realpath behaviour. The ancestor S_ISDIR guard is never shown to be the thing that refuses (a mutant that errors elsewhere is not a kill).
evidence: Ran on Python 3.13.18: `pytest tests/test_m8_n5_g7_archive_custody.py -k 'removed_runbook_guard or custody_faults'` -> 1 failed (ancestor-kind), 19 passed. Debug run of the mutated block with fault=ancestor-kind: rc=1, stderr ends `NotADirectoryError: [Errno 20] Not a directory: .../operator` from `path.resolve(strict=True)` in directory(), line 53 of the program, before ancestors() runs. Same selection on Python 3.12.3: 20 passed. Pre-existing: present in the file's earliest visible history; origin not bisected.

summary: The record-checker grammar test has no refusal case for most of the checker's affirmative guards, so they can be deleted without any test failing.
failure_scenario: RECORDS covers wrong commit, installed:false, different:1, duplicate keys, trailing text, modes and exit lines, but never a controller entry with uid!=0 or state!='tree', first_parent:false, script_matches_commit:false, schema_version!=2, a bool/non-int `different`, a d2 probe with production_available:true or a wrong scope, a d2 verify with installed:false, or an r19 record with files==0. Removing any of those assertions from the Q4 checker leaves all 37 tests green, so an unfaithful record (wrong owner, non-first-parent commit, production-available probe) would be accepted as `*-record-checked` while the suite stays green. q13 reuses this checker via source q12, so it inherits the gap.
evidence: Mutated a copy of docs/plans/handoffs/M8-maintenance-q12-continuation.md (scratch checkout, not the repo) one guard at a time and ran `pytest tests/test_m8_maintenance_q12_continuation.py -k record_checker`: removing entry uid==0, entry state=='tree', first_parent is True, script_matches_commit is True, schema_version==2, probe production_available is False, probe scope==..., d2 verify installed is True, r19 files>0, and type(different) is int each left `37 passed`. All ten SURVIVED.

summary: The g10 floor-9 test sets both qualification records to the same floor, so a checker that reads only one of them passes; the g9/g11 siblings vary each record independently.
failure_scenario: test_generation_ten_publication_requires_both_strict_floor_nine_records writes the same `floor` value into s4-qualification.json and s6a-qualification.json. If C4's loop is narrowed to s4 only, a s6a record with floor 8, bool or float still lets `publish`/`activate g10` proceed. The test cannot see it because s6a is valid exactly when s4 is. test_both_strict_floors_bind_before_publication (session) and test_both_strict_floor_ten_facts_precede_any_publish (g11) both parametrize `record` to vary one file at a time; this one does not, though its name claims both are bound.
evidence: Mutated a scratch copy of M8-maintenance-private-continuation.md C4 so the loop is `for name in ("s4-qualification.json",):` and ran `pytest tests/test_m8_maintenance_private_continuation.py -k floor` -> `5 passed` (mutant survived). Compared with the g11 test's `record` parameter at tests/test_m8_maintenance_g11_continuation.py:375-377. Pre-existing; origin not bisected.

summary: Several L0 custody checks in the capture and boundary programs have no refusing test: the private-parent mode, the single-link check on captured files, and extra keys in status.json.
failure_scenario: All captures use a 0700 parent, every captured file has nlink==1, and the only status.json damage is a duplicate key. So (a) a group/world-accessible LANES parent, (b) a stdout/stderr/status file hard-linked elsewhere by the captured command, and (c) status.json {"returncode":0,"extra":...} are never offered to the capture or lane_boundary. Deleting those guards leaves the suite green, so the boundary that is supposed to refuse a non-private or aliased or non-closed capture would accept it and print lane-boundary-checked.
evidence: Mutated a scratch copy of M8-maintenance-lane-output.md (the L0 block the tests execute): dropping `info.st_mode & 0o077 == 0` from capture's parent check and dropping `opened.st_nlink == 1` from capture's identity loop each left `pytest tests/test_m8_lane_output.py -k 'capture or occupied or unstartable or stderr_bound or status_bound'` at `18 passed`. Dropping `set(status) == {"returncode"}` from lane_boundary left `-k 'test_real_cli_output or every_deviation'` at `54 passed`. All three SURVIVED. The existing DAMAGE list covers status-duplicate and status-missing but not an extra key. Pre-existing; origin not bisected.

summary: The pin-guard half of test_diagnosis_shell_blocks_parse_and_unprepared_pins_stop only drives refusal, and it overwrites the real pins with UNREVIEWED first, so it cannot tell a correct guard from one that always refuses.
failure_scenario: The test replaces EVIDENCE_SHA256/DIAGNOSTIC_SHA256 with UNREVIEWED and leaves EXPECTED_BOOT=UNREVIEWED, then asserts a silent non-zero exit. A guard that fails for every input, including a well-formed 64-hex pin or a real boot UUID, passes. No test runs these guards with valid literals and expects them to continue, contrary to the repo's rule to test the accepting path.
evidence: Replaced `[[ "$EVIDENCE_SHA256" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]` and the EXPECTED_BOOT UUID regex check with `false` in a scratch copy of M8-maintenance-diagnosis.md; `pytest tests/test_m8_maintenance_diagnosis.py -k unprepared_pins` stayed `1 passed` for both. The transport-verifier tests do accept a real boot, but they run a separate Python verifier, not these shell guards.

summary: The LINUX marker only checks sys.platform, so running the Linux-only launch-host tests as root produces dozens of misleading failures instead of a skip or a named precondition.
failure_scenario: The stager refuses to run as root, and the fixture's lstat shim only fabricates a root-owned view for non-root callers. Under root (a normal container user) every LaunchHost test fails at `staged()` with an opaque `assert 1 == 0` on a long record, and refusal tests cannot be told apart from setup failure. The fixture fails when its precondition is false, but never names it.
evidence: As root on Linux, `pytest tests/test_m8_host_runtime.py` -> 78 failed (staging step: stage-launch returns status 1). As a non-root user with umask 022 on Python 3.12.3, the same file plus the g7 file -> 245 passed, 4 skipped. This is an environment precondition, not an authority defect.

summary: Host-runtime launch tests (tests/test_m8_host_runtime.py) pass as a non-root user on Python 3.12; they cover both acceptance (full stage/judge/install/verify and replacement-keeps-store) and refusal, and mutating retirement identity checks is covered by the substituted-store and forged-record tests.

Lane-output strict-bound tests (stderr 8192, status 64) bind at their limit with accepting and refusing inputs, and the stderr/exit guard-removal regressions fail by AssertionError matching the damage id (a real kill, not an error).

The g11/session floor, H7 control-order, capture-descriptor, identity-loss and quiescence tests each include an accepting case and per-record or per-control refusals; the g11 capture identity guard-removal regression asserts the specific refusal message.

Apart from the g7 ancestor-kind mutation proof on Python 3.13 and the root-only host-runtime failures, every assigned test file passed when run (Python 3.13 as root for most files; host-runtime and g7 on Python 3.12 as non-root).
